ranked.headline: Graph neural networks extend molecular property prediction to CNS, toxicity and cliffs
ranked.summary: Recent reports extend graph-based molecular models to beyond-Rule-of-5 CNS penetration, activity cliffs, and debiased interaction benchmarks.

ranked.headline: Sequence-based models increasingly prioritize non-coding and rare functional variants
ranked.summary: Protein language models, expression-noise atlases, and region-specific score thresholds now extend variant interpretation beyond mean effects.

ranked.headline: Modeling subject-specific structure in EEG, ECoG, SEEG and connectome representations
ranked.summary: Recent work models inter-subject variability explicitly rather than averaging it out, spanning a published ECoG alignment study and multiple preprints.

ranked.headline: Computational inference of cell identity and spatial layout from transcriptomic data
ranked.summary: Deep learning and statistical models are now being paired with single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data to resolve cell types and tissue organization across…

ranked.headline: Learned embeddings drive protein interaction, binding affinity and structure prediction
ranked.summary: Protein language model embeddings and graph networks are now applied to interaction, affinity and RNA structure prediction in recent preprints.

ranked.headline: Large-scale enumeration of microbial plasmids, enzymes, peptides and genome variants
ranked.summary: Large sequence collections now carry host, structural, and functional annotation across soil, deep-sea, and fermented-food microbiomes.

ranked.headline: Shared latent spaces reconcile unpaired spatial and single-cell omics modalities
ranked.summary: Spatial and single-cell modalities often lack paired measurements, prompting recent contrastive, adversarial, and optimal-transport alignment methods.

ranked.headline: Sparse Bayesian and kernel models infer structure from high-dimensional omics data
ranked.summary: Sparse, interpretable estimators are needed as single-cell and time-series omics grow in dimension and noise.

ranked.headline: Sequence-derived inference of microbial carriage, transmission, and sampling bias
ranked.summary: Genome-resolved metagenomics now feeds transmission models and surveillance comparisons, while primer and metadata biases bound what these inferences capture.

ranked.headline: GPU, SIMD, and workflow engineering target throughput across sequence analysis stages
ranked.summary: Recent papers and preprints report faster alignment, simulation, and methylation analysis, along with reproducible workflows for high-volume sequencing data.

ranked.headline: Minute-scale scRNA-seq resolves NF-κB response bifurcation for dynamic modeling
ranked.summary: Minute-resolution single-cell profiling now places dynamical models directly on observed response trajectories.

ranked.headline: Haplotype-resolved reference genomes and population panels refine variant interpretation
ranked.summary: Gapless T2T assemblies and multiomic population cohorts now supply the reference sequences needed for accurate genomic interpretation.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale and network models infer metabolic regulation from multi-omic data
ranked.summary: Multi-omic and constraint-based models now resolve metabolic regulation at subject, cell, and tumor-type resolution across cancer and gut disease.

ranked.headline: Pretrained embeddings with capsule and contrastive learning target modification sites
ranked.summary: Recent 2025 studies pair protein and RNA language-model embeddings with capsule, contrastive, and siamese objectives for site-level prediction on biomolecular…

ranked.headline: Information-theoretic measures and reproducible R workflows for omics analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications release open-source R/Bioconductor and command-line tools for surprisal, multi-omics, and spatial workflows.

ranked.headline: DNA sequence and nucleosome features jointly govern chromatin structure and methylation
ranked.summary: Multiscale models and sequence-based deep learning now treat chromatin determinants from condensates to single CpG methylation sites.

ranked.headline: Model form and calibration choices shape inference in epidemic and biological simulations
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published package expose how model structure, reward design, and ABC calibration affect fitted epidemic and therapy predictions.

ranked.headline: Language models steer generative design of proteins and genomic sequences
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs generative sequence models with structural, evolutionary, and genomic context to design functional proteins and genes.

ranked.headline: Sequence-based deep learning predicts protein binding affinity and interaction interfaces
ranked.summary: Protein language model embeddings now serve as sequence-only inputs for binding affinity and interface prediction in recent studies.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking expression forecasting and proteomics workflows against simple baselines
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks show most expression forecasting methods fail to beat simple baselines, prompting closer scrutiny of analysis workflow choices.

ranked.headline: Ensemble-based analysis of protein flexibility across simulation and experimental data
ranked.summary: Flexibility is now analyzed directly across conformational ensembles from MD, BioEmu, AlphaFold2, and AFM-derived reconstructions.

ranked.headline: Explicit gene and disease networks are used to rank candidate targets and disease modules
ranked.summary: Structured biological networks are increasingly coupled to candidate ranking and to systematic benchmarking across gene regulation and disease modules.

ranked.headline: Open-source packages and inference methods for calibrating mechanistic biological models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications pair mechanistic modelling with machine learning to calibrate biological models from noisy, multi-lab data.

ranked.headline: Pretrained DNA encoders predict cell type-specific chromatin architecture and expression
ranked.summary: Recent work extends pretrained DNA models to chromatin conformation data and long-range regulatory benchmarks.

ranked.headline: Models resolve disordered-protein binding, oligomer stability, and allosteric dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study apply MD, Markov state, and polymer models to disordered and dynamic protein systems.

ranked.headline: Higher-order and topological models of brain networks from fMRI and transcriptomic data
ranked.summary: Topological and higher-order formulations now capture brain organization beyond pairwise edges, testing group differences and co-expression discontinuities.

ranked.headline: Open pipelines automate binder design, docking, and coarse-grained protein topology…
ranked.summary: Recent open-source releases package binder design, virtual screening, and coarse-grained topology generation into automated, modular workflows.

ranked.headline: New tools for Y-haplogroup calling, assembly QC, Z-DNA and LD mapping
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications introduce open computational tools for genome-scale variant, assembly, and structural DNA analysis.

ranked.headline: Structure-conditioned diffusion and flow models generate 3D ligands and peptides
ranked.summary: Apo-to-holo pocket generation, all-atom neural field models, and human-in-the-loop flow matching are now appearing in preprints for 3D ligand design.

ranked.headline: Symbolic, thermodynamic, and fitting tools for dynamic reaction and pathway models
ranked.summary: Automating symbolic bifurcation analysis, thermodynamic constraints, and kinetic fitting makes mechanistic dynamic models more tractable across systems.

ranked.headline: Omitted epistasis distorts GWAS null test statistics while association scope broadens
ranked.summary: Expanding GWAS to multivariate and molecular phenotypes raises the stakes for null-distribution validity under unmodeled epistasis.

ranked.headline: Computational inference of RNA and DNA-protein interactions from sequence and read data
ranked.summary: Crowd-built benchmarks and reference-free pipelines are testing how far computational models can recover binding and splicing from raw data.

ranked.headline: Multiscale models couple cell mechanics, membrane lipids and immune priming in cancer
ranked.summary: Three recent items apply mechanistic simulation to cancer at vaccine, cell-migration and membrane scales, spanning PBPK, hybrid FSI and molecular dynamics.

ranked.headline: Learning-rule models linked to decision and response-time behavior
ranked.summary: Coupling explicit learning-rule structure to response-time behavior is emerging as a way to discriminate candidate learning mechanisms.

ranked.headline: LLM agents query genomic, cohort, and kinetic model resources via natural language
ranked.summary: Open-source LLMs served locally now drive curated genomic, cohort, and simulation resources, with early benchmark and tool evidence.

ranked.headline: Demography and chromosome fusions shape genome evolution and lineage coupling
ranked.summary: Simulation-based Ks calibration and genome-wide coupling estimates now test how demography and rearrangements shape lineage divergence.

ranked.headline: Polynomial-time and exact graph algorithms for phylogenetic and pangenome networks
ranked.summary: Recent preprints supply exact and scalable combinatorial algorithms for network-structured genomic data beyond trees.

ranked.headline: Delays, size and frequency set resonance and synchrony regimes in coupled oscillators
ranked.summary: Analytical and simulation studies now link propagation delay, network size and frequency allocation directly to resonance and synchronization regimes.

ranked.headline: Noise, dispersal and nutrient stoichiometry shape ecological equilibria and synchrony
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply analytically tractable reductions to stochastic ecological models of synchrony, nutrient limitation and sparse interaction networks.
